definition_zh: 椅子；主席；主持人；（会议的）主席席位
definition_en: a seat with a back for one person; the person who leads a meeting or group
core_image: 一把有靠背的椅子，或坐在最前排主持会议的那个人
scene: 教室里，同学们搬来椅子准备开会，班主任坐在最前面主持。Please bring a chair to the meeting room.
sceneCN: 这里 chair 是「椅子」（第 1 个义项：有靠背的单人坐具）；句意为请搬一把椅子到会议室。

derivatives.zh: 由 chair 加 man 构成，义为「主席；董事长」
chair 的中性说法，义为「主席（不分性别）」
由 chair 加 woman 构成，义为「女主席」

senses.title: A seat with a back for one person
senses.definition: a piece of furniture for one person to sit on, with a back and usually four legs
senses.definitionCN: 供一人坐的家具，有靠背，通常有四条腿
senses.example: She pulled up a chair and sat next to me.
senses.exampleCN: 她拉过一把椅子，坐在我旁边。
senses.why: The oldest sense names the object itself: a backrest seat is the basic picture of the word.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项直接命名器物：一张带靠背的座位就是这个词最基本的画面。

senses.title: The person who runs a meeting or group
senses.definition: the person in charge of a meeting, committee or organization
senses.definitionCN: 负责主持会议、委员会或组织的人
senses.example: The chair announced the results of the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 主席宣布了投票结果。
senses.why: The seat at the head of the table belongs to the leader, so the seat's name was given to the person sitting in it.
senses.whyCN: 桌首的座位属于领头人，于是这个座位的名字转指坐在上面的人。

senses.title: The position of chairperson itself
senses.definition: the official position of being the chair of a group
senses.definitionCN: 在团体中担任主席这一正式职位
senses.example: He has held the chair of the student union for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 他担任学生会主席已经两年。
senses.why: Once the person is called the chair, the role itself can also borrow the same name.
senses.whyCN: 人既然可以被称为 chair，这个职位本身也顺理成章借用了同一个名字。

senses.title: A professor's post at a university
senses.titleCN: 大学教授职位；讲座教席
senses.definition: a permanent post as a senior university professor
senses.definitionCN: 大学里资深教授的固定职位
senses.example: She was appointed to the chair of chemistry at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她被聘任为这所大学的化学讲座教授。
senses.why: Universities also use a 'seat' of learning for their top teaching posts, extending the meeting-room image.
senses.whyCN: 大学把最高教席也看成一张「座位」，把会议室的画面延伸到了学术界。

intro.en: Chair travelled from a Greek word for a seat through Latin and Old French before reaching English.
intro.cn: chair 从希腊语中指「座位」的词出发，经拉丁语和古法语一路传入英语。

items.en: Greek kathedra meant a seat, built on kata (down) and hedra (seat, base).
items.cn: 希腊语 kathedra 指座位，由 kata（向下）加 hedra（座位、基座）构成。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as cathedra, keeping the sense of a seat, especially an official one.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 cathedra，仍指座位，尤指正式的席位。

items.en: Old French turned it into chaire, later chaere, meaning a seat of authority.
items.cn: 古法语演变为 chaire、chaere，指权威者的座位。

items.en: Middle English took the word as chaiere, first for high seats, then for ordinary chairs.
items.cn: 中古英语作 chaiere，先指高位座椅，后泛指普通椅子。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the furniture sense and the leader sense of chair.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了 chair 的家具义和「主持人」义。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects other kinds of seats and leaders.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收其他坐具和主持类词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「头发」，拼写与 chair 接近。

entries.definition: A series of metal rings joined together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「链条」，词首与 chair 相近。

entries.definition: To shout with joy or support.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欢呼；鼓舞」，读音与 chair 开头相近。

entries.definition: A seat without a back or arms.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「凳子」，与椅子同为坐具但无靠背。

entries.definition: A long seat for several people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「长凳」，可坐多人。

entries.definition: The person who leads an organization or country.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「主席；总统」，与 chair 的主持义相近。

abstract.cn: 想象四条稳稳的腿撑起一片靠背，托住你疲惫的后背。

abstract.en: Hear the scrape of the chair as the meeting goes quiet.
abstract.cn: 会议安静下来时，仿佛听见椅子挪动的刮擦声。

abstract.en: Feel the head seat at the table pulling all eyes to it.
abstract.cn: 感受桌首那把椅子如何把所有目光吸引过去。

examples.en: Please bring a chair for our guest.
examples.cn: 请给客人搬一把椅子来。

examples.en: Who will chair the class meeting tomorrow?
examples.cn: 明天班会由谁来主持？

examples.en: An empty chair stood by the window.
examples.cn: 窗边立着一把空椅子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「切尔」——且把耳朵靠上椅背休息，切尔坐上椅子。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form cathedra lives on in several English words.

definition_zh: 粉笔；白垩；用粉笔写（或画）
definition_en: soft white limestone used for writing; a stick of this material; to write with it
core_image: 一支白色粉笔在黑板上沙沙作响，留下白色痕迹
scene: 数学课前，值日生把三支白色粉笔放到讲台上。The teacher wrote the date on the board with a piece of chalk.
sceneCN: 这里 chalk 是「粉笔」（第 1 个义项：能在黑板上写字的白条）；句意为老师用粉笔在黑板上写日期。

derivatives.zh: 由 chalk 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「白垩质的；发白的」
由 chalk 加 board 构成，义为「黑板」

senses.title: A stick for writing on a blackboard
senses.definition: a small stick of soft white material used for writing or drawing, especially on a blackboard
senses.definitionCN: 用软白材料做的小条，用来写字画画，尤指在黑板上
senses.example: He broke the chalk while writing quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 他写得太快，把粉笔折断了。
senses.why: The writing stick is the everyday object named directly by the material it is made of.
senses.whyCN: 写字用的条状物直接以制材命名，因为它由这种白色软石做成。

senses.title: The soft white rock itself
senses.definition: a type of soft white limestone rock, formed from ancient sea creatures
senses.definitionCN: 一种白色软质石灰岩，由远古海洋生物形成
senses.example: The cliffs at Dover are made of white chalk.
senses.exampleCN: 多佛的悬崖由白色白垩构成。
senses.why: Before the stick, the rock itself carried the name; the stick is just the rock shaped for writing.
senses.whyCN: 先有岩石之名，后才有粉笔条；条不过是把这种岩石削成了写字的形状。

senses.title: To write or draw with chalk
senses.definition: to write or draw something using chalk
senses.definitionCN: 用粉笔写字或画画
senses.example: Someone chalked a smiley face on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 有人在墙上用粉笔画了个笑脸。
senses.why: Materials often turn into verbs for using them, so the white stick also names the act of writing with it.
senses.whyCN: 材料名常转为使用它的动词，白条便也命名了用它书写的动作。

intro.en: Chalk goes back to a Latin word for lime or limestone, arriving in English through Germanic languages.
intro.cn: chalk 的源头是拉丁语中指「石灰」的词，经日耳曼诸语传入英语。

items.en: Latin calx meant limestone or lime, from a Greek word for pebble.
items.cn: 拉丁语 calx 指石灰岩或石灰，源自一个指卵石的希腊词。

items.en: Old English cealc meant chalk or lime, borrowed from Latin via Germanic tribes.
items.cn: 古英语 cealc 指白垩或石灰，经日耳曼部落由拉丁语借入。

items.en: In Middle English, chalk named both the white rock and the writing stick.
items.cn: 中古英语里，chalk 既指白色岩层，也指写字的白条。

items.en: As schools spread, chalk became firmly linked to blackboard writing.
items.cn: 随着学校普及，chalk 与黑板书写牢固地联系起来。

items.en: Today chalk covers the writing stick, the white rock, and the verb of writing with it.
items.cn: 今天 chalk 涵盖粉笔条、白垩岩，以及用它书写的动词。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects related writing materials.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收相关书写材料类词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脸颊」，读音与 chalk 相近。

entries.definition: To examine something to make sure it is right.

entries.definition: A stick of coloured wax for drawing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜡笔」，同为书写画画的条状物。

entries.definition: A felt-tip pen for writing on boards.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「记号笔」，在现代教室常代替粉笔。
名词，义为「石灰」，与 chalk 同源于拉丁语 calx。

abstract.en: Picture a white cliff rising straight out of the sea.
abstract.cn: 想象白色悬崖从海面笔直升起。

abstract.en: Feel the tiny dust settling on your fingers after class.
abstract.cn: 下课后感受指尖落下的细小粉尘。

examples.en: Someone chalked a big heart on the playground wall.
examples.cn: 有人在操场墙上用粉笔画了一颗大爱心。

definition_zh: 挑战；难题；质疑；向……挑战；质疑
definition_en: a demanding task that tests ability; an invitation to compete; to question the truth of something
core_image: 有人把战书掷到你面前，要你应战或接受考验
scene: 运动会上，隔壁班向我们班下了长跑比赛的战书。The relay race was a real challenge for our team.
sceneCN: 这里 challenge 是「挑战；难题」（第 1 个义项：考验能力的困难任务）；句意为接力赛对我们队是真正的挑战。

derivatives.zh: 由 challenge 加 -ing 构成，义为「有挑战性的；困难的」
由 challenge 加 -er 构成，义为「挑战者」

senses.title: A demanding task that tests ability
senses.definition: a difficult task or problem that tests someone's ability or effort
senses.definitionCN: 考验能力或努力的困难任务或问题
senses.example: Learning a new language is a big challenge.
senses.exampleCN: 学习一门新语言是个大挑战。
senses.why: The old contest call became a name for any hard task, because a hard task also dares you to try.
senses.whyCN: 古老的叫阵声变成了困难任务的代名词，因为困难同样在向你的能力叫板。

senses.title: An invitation to compete or fight
senses.definition: an invitation to take part in a contest or fight to see who is better
senses.definitionCN: 邀请参加比赛或较量，看谁更强
senses.example: He threw down a challenge to a chess game after school.
senses.exampleCN: 他下战后书，约对方放学后下一盘棋。
senses.why: This is the word's oldest sense: formally calling someone out to prove who wins.
senses.whyCN: 这是词的最古老义项：正式叫人出来一决高下。

senses.title: To question the truth or rightness of something
senses.definition: to say that something may not be true or right, and ask for proof
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事未必真实或正确，要求拿出证据
senses.example: She challenged the answer and asked the teacher to check it again.
senses.exampleCN: 她质疑那个答案，请老师再核对一次。
senses.why: To challenge someone once meant to accuse them, so questioning a claim is like calling it to defend itself.
senses.whyCN: challenge 曾指指控某人，质疑一个说法就像叫它出来自证。

senses.title: To invite someone to compete
senses.definition: to formally ask someone to compete against you
senses.definitionCN: 正式邀请某人与自己比赛
senses.example: Our class challenged Class Two to a basketball match.
senses.exampleCN: 我们班向二班发起篮球比赛挑战。
senses.why: The contest call itself became a verb: to challenge is to give the call.
senses.whyCN: 叫阵的名词本身转为动词：challenge 就是发出叫阵。

intro.en: Challenge comes from a Latin word for calling someone out by name, passing through Old French into English.
intro.cn: challenge 源自拉丁语中指「点名叫出某人」的词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Latin calumnia meant a false accusation or legal claim, later shaped into calumniari, to accuse falsely.
items.cn: 拉丁语 calumnia 指诬告或法律指控，后形成动词 calumniari（诬告）。

items.en: Old French chalonge meant a claim, complaint or accusation in law.
items.cn: 古法语 chalonge 指法律上的主张、控诉或申诉。

items.en: Middle English chalenge first meant to accuse or claim something as one's right.
items.cn: 中古英语 chalenge 先指指控或主张某种权利。

items.en: The sense shifted to calling someone out to a contest or duel.
items.cn: 词义转为叫人出来比赛或决斗。

items.en: Modern English uses challenge for contests, hard tasks and questioning claims.
items.cn: 现代英语的 challenge 涵盖比赛、难题和质疑之义。

definition_zh: 冠军；优胜者；拥护者；捍卫者；为……而战；支持
definition_en: a person or team that wins first place; someone who defends a cause; to support strongly
core_image: 领奖台上举起奖杯的第一名，或为一个目标挺身而出的人
scene: 全校运动会的领奖台上，我们班的长跑冠军高高举起了奖杯。Our class runner became the school champion in the 800-metre race.
sceneCN: 这里 champion 是「冠军」（第 1 个义项：比赛获得第一名的人）；句意为我们班的运动员成为校运会八百米冠军。

collocations.zh: 为事业奔走；支持一项事业

derivatives.zh: 由 champion 加 -ship 构成，义为「锦标赛；冠军地位」
由 champion 加后缀构成，义为「没有冠军的」

senses.title: The winner of first place in a contest
senses.definition: a person or team that wins first place in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中获得第一名的人或队伍
senses.example: She is the school swimming champion this year.
senses.exampleCN: 她是今年的校游泳冠军。
senses.why: The one who fights for another side, and wins, naturally becomes the named victor of the field.
senses.whyCN: 替一方出战并获胜的人，自然就成了赛场上被命名的胜者。

senses.title: A person who fights or speaks for a cause
senses.definition: someone who strongly supports and defends a person, idea or group
senses.definitionCN: 坚定支持并捍卫某人、某想法或某团体的人
senses.example: He is a champion of cleaner rivers in our city.
senses.exampleCN: 他是本市洁净河流的坚定捍卫者。
senses.why: The word's oldest meaning was a fighter who took your place in battle, so any brave defender keeps this name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的含义是替你上阵的战士，因此一切勇敢的捍卫者都保留了这个名字。

senses.title: To support or defend publicly
senses.definition: to publicly support a cause, person or plan
senses.definitionCN: 公开支持某项事业、某人或某个计划
senses.example: The student union championed the plan for a reading corner.
senses.exampleCN: 学生会大力支持设立读书角的想法。
senses.why: When the defender keeps fighting for a cause, the fighter's name becomes a verb of supporting it.
senses.whyCN: 捍卫者持续为某项事业而战，战士之名便转成支持该事业的动词。

senses.title: A title or award for winning
senses.definition: the title given to the winner of a championship
senses.definitionCN: 授予锦标赛获胜者的称号
senses.example: The team held the champion title for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍连续三年保持冠军称号。
senses.why: The winner's name itself can stand for the prize and title attached to the win.
senses.whyCN: 胜者的名字本身也可以代指胜利带来的奖赏与头衔。

intro.en: Champion goes back to a Late Latin word for a battlefield fighter, reaching English through Old French.
intro.cn: champion 可追溯到晚期拉丁语中指「战场战士」的词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Late Latin campio meant a fighter or duelist, built on campus, a field of battle.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 campio 指战士或决斗者，源于 campus（战场、原野）。

items.en: Old French champion meant a champion or defender, one who fights for another.
items.cn: 古法语 champion 指冠军或捍卫者，即替人出战之人。

items.en: Middle English took champion for a fighter in single combat or a defender.
items.cn: 中古英语用 champion 指单挑的斗士或捍卫者。

items.en: The sense narrowed to a winner in contests and games.
items.cn: 词义收窄，专指比赛中的获胜者。

items.en: Today champion names first-place winners, loyal defenders, and the act of supporting.
items.cn: 今天 champion 既指第一名、捍卫者，也指支持的行动。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects winners and supporters.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收优胜者与支持者类词。

abstract.en: Hear your name called as the last flag is crossed.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见冲过终点旗时自己名字被念响。

abstract.en: Feel the steady heart of someone guarding a cause alone.
abstract.cn: 感受一个人独自守护某项事业时那颗坚定的心。

examples.en: Our class runner became the school champion in the 800-metre race.
examples.cn: 我们班的运动员成为校运会八百米冠军。

examples.en: She is a champion of animal rights in our school.
examples.cn: 她是学校里动物权益的坚定捍卫者。

examples.en: The students championed the idea of a school garden.
examples.cn: 学生们大力支持建校园花园的想法。

definition_zh: 收费；控告；充电；冲锋；负责；指责；电荷
definition_en: to ask money for something; to accuse; to fill a battery; a rush forward; the duty of looking after something
core_image: 一手收钱记账，一手举刀冲锋，中间还有蓄电与控告
scene: 小卖部老板帮弟弟的充电宝补满电，顺手收了他两块钱。The shop owner charged two yuan for filling the power bank.
sceneCN: 这里 charge 是「收费」（第 1 个义项：为服务或物品要钱）；句意为店主给充电宝充电收了两块钱。

pos.zh: 费用；控告；电荷；主管职责

derivatives.zh: 由 charge 加 -er 构成，义为「充电器」
由 re- 加 charge 构成，义为「再充电；恢复精力」
由 charge 变形构成，义为「带电的；气氛紧张的」

senses.title: To ask money for goods or a service
senses.definition: to ask for or take money as payment for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某物或某项服务索取金钱
senses.example: The shop owner charged two yuan for the repair.
senses.exampleCN: 店主收了两块钱修理费。
senses.why: A load placed on someone once meant an obligation to pay, so putting a price on service became the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 加在某人身上的「负荷」曾指付款义务，给服务定价便成了日常义。

senses.title: To accuse someone of doing wrong
senses.definition: to officially say that someone has done something wrong or illegal
senses.definitionCN: 正式指称某人做了错事或违法行为
senses.example: The police charged him with taking the bike.
senses.exampleCN: 警方指控他拿走了自行车。
senses.why: A charge was also a burden laid on a person, and an accusation loads guilt onto someone like a weight.
senses.whyCN: charge 也指压在人身上的担子，指控就像把罪责这个重物压到人身上。

senses.title: To fill a battery with electricity
senses.definition: to put electricity into a battery or device
senses.definitionCN: 把电输入电池或设备
senses.example: Remember to charge your tablet before class.
senses.exampleCN: 上课前记得给平板电脑充电。
senses.why: Filling a battery is loading power into it, the same picture of putting a load into something.
senses.whyCN: 充电就是把电力「装进」设备，与「把负荷装入某物」是同一画面。

senses.title: To rush forward to attack
senses.definition: to run quickly and directly towards someone or something, especially to attack
senses.definitionCN: 快速径直冲向某人或某物，尤指发起攻击
senses.example: The dog charged at the ball and grabbed it.
senses.exampleCN: 狗朝球猛冲过去，一把叼住。
senses.why: A charge in battle is a loaded rush with all one's force, extending 'load' to 'full-speed attack'.
senses.whyCN: 战场上的冲锋是倾尽全力的突袭，把「装载」延伸为「全速突进」。

senses.title: The duty of looking after someone or something
senses.definition: the responsibility given to someone to control or care for something
senses.definitionCN: 交给某人掌管或照看某事的责任
senses.example: Ms Li is in charge of the library.
senses.exampleCN: 李老师负责管理图书馆。
senses.why: The load handed to a person becomes the responsibility itself, so being in charge is carrying that load.
senses.whyCN: 交付给某人的负荷就成了责任本身，in charge 即挑起这副担子。

senses.title: A price asked for something
senses.definition: an amount of money asked for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 为商品或服务索要的金额
senses.example: The delivery charge is five yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 送货费是五块钱。
senses.why: The act of asking money turns into the money asked, a normal shift from action to result.
senses.whyCN: 索取金钱的行为转为所索的金额，是常见的由动作转结果。

senses.title: Electric energy stored in a battery or body
senses.definition: the amount of electricity stored or carried by something
senses.definitionCN: 某物储存或携带的电量
senses.example: The battery still has some charge left.
senses.exampleCN: 电池里还剩一点电量。
senses.why: What has been loaded into the battery can be named by the loading word itself.
senses.whyCN: 装入电池的东西，就用「装入」这个词来命名。

intro.en: Charge comes from a Late Latin word for loading a cart or horse, reaching English through Old French.
intro.cn: charge 源自晚期拉丁语中「给车马装货」的词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Late Latin carricare meant to load a wheeled vehicle, built on carrus, a cart.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 carricare 指给车装货，源于 carrus（四轮车）。

items.en: Old French chargier meant to load, weigh down or entrust a duty.
items.cn: 古法语 chargier 指装载、压负或托付职责。

items.en: Middle English chargen covered loading, burdening and entrusting responsibilities.
items.cn: 中古英语 chargen 涵装载、负重与托付责任。

items.en: Senses multiplied: prices, accusations, military rushes and duties.
items.cn: 义项倍增：收费、控告、军事冲锋与职责。

items.en: Modern English adds the electrical sense: to charge batteries and speak of electric charge.
items.cn: 现代英语增加电学义：给电池充电、谈论电荷。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects related money and duty words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收费用与职责类词。

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装载」，与 charge 的「装入」义相近。

definition_zh: 机会；可能性；偶然；碰巧；冒险
definition_en: an opportunity to do something; the possibility that something will happen; happening by luck
core_image: 掷出去还没落地的骰子，落点未定，一切皆有可能
scene: 班会选举时，老师鼓励每个同学都给自己一次上台展示的机会。Take this chance to show your talents to the class.
sceneCN: 这里 chance 是「机会」（第 1 个义项：可以做某事的时机）；句意为抓住这次机会向全班展示才华。

derivatives.zh: 由 chance 加 -y 构成，义为「冒险的；不确定的」
由 chance 加 -ful 构成，义为「多变的；靠运气的」

senses.title: An opportunity to do something
senses.definition: a time when you can do something you want to do
senses.definitionCN: 能够做自己想做之事的时机
senses.example: Take this chance to show your talents to the class.
senses.exampleCN: 抓住这次机会向全班展示才华。
senses.why: What falls out is not planned; when events fall your way, that opening is your chance.
senses.whyCN: 掷出的点数并非计划所得；当事情恰好落在你这边，那个时机就是你的机会。

senses.title: The possibility that something will happen
senses.definition: how likely it is that something will happen
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能性大小
senses.example: There is a good chance of rain this afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 今天下午很可能下雨。
senses.why: The fall of the dice measures how likely a thing is, so the falling word names probability itself.
senses.whyCN: 骰子的点数可衡量一件事的倾向，掷落之词便转指可能性本身。

senses.title: Happening by luck, not plan
senses.definition: the way things happen without anyone planning them
senses.definitionCN: 事情在无人安排的情况下发生的方式
senses.example: I met my old friend quite by chance.
senses.exampleCN: 我偶遇了老朋友。
senses.why: What no one arranges belongs to the falling dice: unplanned events are pure chance.
senses.whyCN: 无人安排之事属于掷出的骰子：偶然发生之事就是纯然的 chance。

senses.title: To risk doing something
senses.definition: to risk doing something, hoping it will turn out well
senses.definitionCN: 冒险做某事，希望有好结果
senses.example: We will chance the weather and go cycling.
senses.exampleCN: 我们要赌一把天气，去骑自行车。
senses.why: Trusting to the fall of the dice becomes a verb of daring the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 把结果交给骰子的点数，便化作赌一把的动词。

intro.en: Chance comes from a Latin word for the fall of the dice, passing through French into English.
intro.cn: chance 源自拉丁语中指骰子掷落的词，经法语传入英语。

items.en: Late Latin cadentia meant a falling, built on cadere, to fall.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cadentia 指落下，源于动词 cadere（落下）。

items.en: Old French cheance meant the fall of dice and hence fortune.
items.cn: 古法语 cheance 指骰子的掷落，进而指运气。

items.en: Middle English chance kept the luck sense and grew the opportunity sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 chance 保留运气义，并发展出机会义。

items.en: The possibility sense spread into weather, games and everyday talk.
items.cn: 可能性之义渗入天气、游戏与日常会话。

items.en: Modern English uses chance for opportunity, probability, luck and risky trying.
items.cn: 现代英语的 chance 涵盖机会、可能性、运气与冒险一试。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects luck and opportunity words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收运气与机会类词。

形容词，义为「冒险的」，由 chance 派生。

entries.definition: A chance to do something good.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「良机」，与 chance 的机会义相近。

entries.definition: Good or bad fortune that comes without planning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「运气」，与 chance 的偶然义相近。

entries.definition: The danger that something bad may happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「风险」，与 chance 的冒险义相关。

normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 chance。

normal.en: chance comes from Latin cadere, to fall.
normal.cn: chance 源自拉丁语 cadere（落下）。

normal.en: cadence, the rhythm of music, shares the same falling root.
normal.cn: cadence（节奏）与 chance 同享「落下」词根。

normal.en: by chance means without planning.
normal.cn: by chance 意为偶然、无意中。

normal.en: take a chance means to risk it.
normal.cn: take a chance 意为冒险一试。

normal.en: a slim chance means it is not likely.
normal.cn: a slim chance 意为希望渺茫。

abstract.en: Picture dice tumbling through the air before they land.
abstract.cn: 想象骰子落地前在空中翻滚。

abstract.en: Hear the soft clatter of dice on a wooden table.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见骰子落在木桌上的轻响。

abstract.en: Feel a door swinging open just as you reach it.
abstract.cn: 感受赶到时门恰好为你敞开的瞬间。

examples.en: Take this chance to show your talents to the class.
examples.cn: 抓住这次机会向全班展示才华。

examples.en: I met my old friend quite by chance.
examples.cn: 我纯属偶然遇到了老朋友。

examples.en: There is a good chance of rain this afternoon.
examples.cn: 今天下午很可能下雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「强斯」——强手也要看时运，机会来了别错过。

root: 拉丁语 cadere（落下）→ 晚期拉丁语 cadentia（掷落）→ 古法语 cheance → 中古英语 chance → 现代英语 chance；同根词有 cadence（节奏）、accident（事故）、incident（事件）。

sensesIntro.en: Chance falls from the dice into opportunity, probability, luck and risky trying.
sensesIntro.cn: chance 自骰子的掷落延伸出机会、可能性、运气与冒险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dice still in the air
core.cn: 核心意象：尚在空中翻滚的骰子

intro.en: Chance keeps the Latin falling root cad- inside its short frame.
intro.cn: chance 短小的词形里保留了拉丁语「落下」词根 cad-。

latinIntro.en: The root cadere also gives English accident and cadence.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 cadere 还派生出 accident 与 cadence。

items.example: The dice fell to give the chance.

items.meaning: something that happens by chance, often bad
items.example: He was late because of an accident.

items.meaning: an event, especially an unusual one
items.example: The police looked into the incident.

items.meaning: the rise and fall of a rhythm
items.example: She read the poem with a lovely cadence.
Cycling there is chancy in winter.
items.exampleCN: 冬天在那儿骑车有风险。

items.example: We met by chance at the library.
Take a chance and join the team.
Do not miss the chance to thank her.

latinEntries.meaning: a falling, the fall of dice

definition_zh: 改变；更换；交换；零钱；找零；变化
definition_en: to make or become different; to replace one thing with another; money in small coins; the money returned after paying
core_image: 把旧硬币换成新纸币，或换下旧校服换上新装
scene: 换季了，周末妈妈帮我把秋装收进柜子，换上冬装。Mom helped me change my clothes for the colder weather.
sceneCN: 这里 change 是「更换」（第 2 个义项：以新换旧）；句意为妈妈帮我换上了保暖的冬装。

derivatives.zh: 由 change 加 -able 构成，义为「易变的；可变的」
由 ex- 加 change 构成，义为「交换；交易」
由 change 加 over 构成，义为「转换；变更」

senses.title: To make or become different
senses.definition: to make someone or something different, or to become different
senses.definitionCN: 使不同，或自身变得不同
senses.example: Autumn changes the colour of the leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天改变了树叶的颜色。
senses.why: The old sense of trading places, time after time, grows into the general idea of becoming other.
senses.whyCN: 古义指轮换换班，一次次交替便生长为「变为他物」的普遍概念。

senses.title: To replace one thing with another
senses.definition: to take off one thing and put on or use another
senses.definitionCN: 取下一物，换上或改用另一物
senses.example: Mom helped me change my clothes for the colder weather.
senses.exampleCN: 天气转冷，妈妈帮我换上了冬装。
senses.why: Exchanging one for another is the most concrete form of making different.
senses.whyCN: 以一换一正是「使之不同」最具体的形式。

senses.title: To give and receive one thing for another
senses.definition: to give one thing and receive another in return
senses.definitionCN: 交出某物并换取另一物
senses.example: We changed seats so everyone could see.
senses.exampleCN: 我们交换了座位，让每个人都能看见。
senses.why: The oldest sense was barter: two parties each hand over what they hold.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是物物交换：双方各自交出手中之物。

senses.title: Money in small coins
senses.definition: coins of low value, or money in small units
senses.definitionCN: 低面额硬币或小额货币
senses.example: I keep some small change for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我留着些零钱坐公交。
senses.why: Money broken into smaller pieces is 'changed' money, carrying the exchange sense into coins.
senses.whyCN: 被化整为零的钱是「换过」的钱，交换之义便落在了硬币上。

senses.title: The money returned after paying
senses.definition: the money given back when you pay more than the price
senses.definitionCN: 付款超过价格时被退回的钱
senses.example: Here is your change, sir.
senses.exampleCN: 先生，这是找您的零钱。
senses.why: The seller exchanges what you gave for what is owed back, the last echo of barter.
senses.whyCN: 卖家把你多付的换回应退的款项，是物物交换的最后回声。

intro.en: Change comes from a Late Latin word for exchanging, arriving through Old French.
intro.cn: change 源自晚期拉丁语中指交换的词，经古法语传入英语。

items.en: Late Latin cambiare meant to exchange, to barter one thing for another.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cambiare 指交换、以物易物。

items.en: Old French changier meant to exchange, replace or alter.
items.cn: 古法语 changier 指交换、替换或更改。

items.en: Middle English chaungen covered altering things and switching roles.
items.cn: 中古英语 chaungen 涵盖改变事物与轮换职位。

items.en: The money senses grew as trade and small coins spread.
items.cn: 随着贸易与硬币普及，钱币诸义生长起来。

items.en: Modern English keeps changing things, coins, and money returned.
items.cn: 现代英语保留改变、硬币与找零诸义。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects altering and money words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收改变与钱币类词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机会」，拼写与 change 仅差一字母。
动词，义为「收费」，拼写与 change 相近。

entries.definition: To give and receive in return.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「交换」，由 change 加 ex- 构成。
动词，义为「改动」，与 change 相近但幅度较小。

entries.definition: To put a new thing in place of an old one.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「替换」，与 change 的更换义相近。
名词，义为「硬币」，与 change 的零钱义相近。

normalIntro.en: Remember change by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 change。

normal.en: change comes from Late Latin cambiare, to exchange.
normal.cn: change 源自晚期拉丁语 cambiare（交换）。

normal.en: exchange is change with the prefix ex-.
normal.cn: exchange 是 change 加前缀 ex-。

normal.en: change your mind means to decide differently.
normal.cn: change your mind 意为改变主意。

normal.en: keep the change is said to keep returned money.
normal.cn: keep the change 用于表示不收回找零。

normal.en: changeable weather changes often.
normal.cn: changeable weather 指多变天气。

abstract.en: Picture green leaves turning gold one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象绿叶一片片染成金色。

abstract.en: Hear coins dropping one after another into a pocket.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见硬币一枚枚落进口袋。

abstract.en: Feel the old uniform giving way to the new one.
abstract.cn: 感受旧校服脱下、新校服上身。

examples.en: Mom helped me change my clothes for the colder weather.
examples.cn: 天气转冷，妈妈帮我换了衣服。

examples.en: Here is your change, sir.
examples.cn: 先生，这是找您的零钱。

examples.en: Autumn changes the colour of the leaves.
examples.cn: 秋天改变了树叶的颜色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「浅之」——换零钱时找的浅浅几枚硬币，就是 change。

root: 晚期拉丁语 cambiare（交换）→ 古法语 changier → 中古英语 chaungen → 现代英语 change；同根词有 exchange（交换）、changeable（易变的）、chameleon（变色龙，经其他途径）。

sensesIntro.en: Change spreads from barter to altering, replacing, coins and returned money.
sensesIntro.cn: change 由物物交换延伸到改变、替换、零钱与找零。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thing handed over, another taken back
core.cn: 核心意象：交出一物，换回另一物

intro.en: Change carries the Late Latin exchange root cambi- through French.
intro.cn: change 经法语承载了晚期拉丁语的交换词根 cambi-。

latinIntro.en: The root cambiare also stands behind exchange and Cambist.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 cambiare 还支撑着 exchange 等词。

items.example: Change began as trading things.

items.meaning: to give and receive in return
items.example: We exchange stamps after class.
Spring weather is changeable.

items.meaning: a switch from one thing to another
items.example: The changeover to summer time is easy.
I need small change for the bus.
Change trains at the next station.

items.meaning: to let the seller keep returned money
items.example: Keep the change, thanks!
The gift is exchangeable within a week.

definition_zh: 性格；品质；人物；角色；汉字；符号
definition_en: the qualities that make a person special; a person in a story; a letter or symbol used in writing
core_image: 故事里那个一眼就能记住的人物，或方方正正的一个汉字
scene: 语文课上，老师让我们分析课文里小男孩的性格特点。The main character in the story is a brave boy.
sceneCN: 这里 character 是「人物；角色」（第 2 个义项：故事中的人）；句意为故事的主人公是个勇敢的男孩。

pos.zh: 性格；品质；人物；角色；文字符号

derivatives.zh: 由 character 加 -ize 构成，义为「描绘……的特征」
由 character 加后缀构成，义为「典型的；特征」

senses.title: The qualities that make a person special
senses.definition: the mix of qualities that makes one person different from others
senses.definitionCN: 使一个人区别于他人的特质组合
senses.example: Hard work and honesty are part of her character.
senses.exampleCN: 勤奋与诚实是她品格的一部分。
senses.why: A tool's engraved mark fixed its identity; a person's qualities are the marks that fix theirs.
senses.whyCN: 刻印是器物的身份标记；人的特质正是标记其身份的「刻痕」。

senses.title: A person in a story or play
senses.definition: a person, animal or figure in a book, film or play
senses.definitionCN: 书、电影或戏剧中出现的人、动物或形象
senses.example: The main character in the story is a brave boy.
senses.exampleCN: 故事的主人公是个勇敢的男孩。
senses.why: The mark that fixes identity was given to the figures whose traits the writer engraves.
senses.whyCN: 用以标记身份的印记，被赋予了作家笔下刻画的形象。

senses.title: A letter, number or symbol used in writing
senses.definition: a letter, number or sign used in writing and printing
senses.definitionCN: 书写与印刷中使用的字母、数字或符号
senses.example: Chinese characters are written in square shapes.
senses.exampleCN: 汉字写成方块形状。
senses.why: Each written sign is a mark carved to fix a sound or meaning, the oldest sense at its most literal.
senses.whyCN: 每个文字符号都是刻下以固定音义的印记，是最古老义项最直接的呈现。

senses.title: A person with an unusual, striking nature
senses.definition: a person whose behaviour is amusing or unusual
senses.definitionCN: 举止有趣或与众不同的人
senses.example: Grandpa is quite a character at family dinners.
senses.exampleCN: 爷爷在家庭聚餐上是个妙趣横生的人物。
senses.why: A person whose qualities are strongly marked stands out like a deep engraving.
senses.whyCN: 特质鲜明之人如深刻的刻痕般引人注目。

intro.en: Character comes from a Greek word for an engraving tool, growing into identity, story figures and written signs.
intro.cn: character 源自希腊语中指刻印工具的词，逐步生长为身份、故事人物与文字符号之义。

items.en: Greek kharakter meant an engraving tool, and the mark it makes.
items.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 指刻印工具及其刻下的印记。

items.en: Late Latin character meant an engraved mark or a written sign.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 character 指刻印的标记或书写的符号。

items.en: Old French caractère carried the mark sense into Europe's languages.
items.cn: 古法语 caractère 把标记之义带入欧洲诸语言。

items.en: Middle English character meant a written sign, then a person's qualities.
items.cn: 中古英语 character 先指文字符号，后指人的品质。

items.en: Modern English uses character for personality, story figures and letters.
items.cn: 现代英语的 character 兼指性格、故事人物与文字。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects people and signs.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收人物与符号类词。

entries.definition: Typical of a person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词/名词，义为「典型的；特征」，由 character 派生。
动词，义为「收费」，读音与 character 词首相近。
名词，义为「宪章」，拼写与 character 词首相近。

entries.definition: The whole nature of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「个性」，与 character 的性格义相近。

entries.definition: A part played in a film or play.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「角色」，与 character 的角色义相近。

entries.definition: A sign that stands for something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「符号」，与 character 的符号义相近。

normalIntro.en: Remember character by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 character。

normal.en: character comes from Greek kharakter, an engraving tool.
normal.cn: character 源自希腊语 kharakter（刻印工具）。

normal.en: characteristic means typical of someone.
normal.cn: characteristic 意为典型的、有特征的。

normal.en: characterize means to describe the qualities of something.
normal.cn: characterize 意为描绘某物的特征。

normal.en: in character means acting as the person really would.
normal.cn: in character 意为符合角色的性格。

normal.en: Chinese characters keep the engraved-mark idea alive.
normal.cn: 汉字保留了「刻印印记」这一意象。

abstract.en: Picture a craftsman cutting letters deep into wood.
abstract.cn: 想象工匠把字母深深刻进木头。

abstract.en: Hear the story reader's voice bring a figure alive.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见讲故事的声音让人物鲜活起来。

abstract.en: Feel the square strokes of a Chinese character under the pen.
abstract.cn: 感受笔下汉字方正的笔画。

examples.en: The main character in the story is a brave boy.
examples.cn: 故事的主人公是个勇敢的男孩。

examples.en: Hard work and honesty are part of her character.
examples.cn: 勤奋与诚实是她品格的一部分。

examples.en: Chinese characters are written in square shapes.
examples.cn: 汉字写成方块形状。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凯瑞克特」——刻瑞特别的印记，刻出人物的性格。

root: 希腊语 kharakter（刻印工具、印记）→ 晚期拉丁语 character → 古法语 caractère → 中古英语 character → 现代英语 character；派生词有 characteristic（典型的）、characterize（描绘特征）。

sensesIntro.en: Character moves from the engraved mark to personality, story figures and written signs.
sensesIntro.cn: character 由刻印的印记延伸到品格、故事人物与文字符号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark cut deep enough to fix identity
core.cn: 核心意象：深深刻下、足以固定身份的印记

intro.en: Character carries the Greek engraving root kharakt- into English.
intro.cn: character 把希腊语刻印词根 kharakt- 带入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Late Latin character is the direct bridge.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 character 是直接的桥梁。

items.example: A character is a mark of identity.

items.meaning: typical of a person or thing
items.example: Red cheeks are characteristic of her.
The novel characterizes village life.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说描绘了乡村生活。

items.meaning: an actor of special, unusual roles
items.example: He is a famous character actor.
Her joke was in character.
items.exampleCN: 她开玩笑符合她一贯的作风。

items.example: His anger was out of character.
items.exampleCN: 他发火不像他平日的为人。

items.example: Team sports are good for character building.
items.exampleCN: 团体运动有助于品格培养。

items.example: The street was grey and characterless.

definition_zh: 图表；海图；航行图；排行榜；绘制图表
definition_en: a sheet giving facts in the form of pictures, lines or tables; a map for sailors; to make a chart of
core_image: 一张纸上用线条和图形把数字讲清楚，或一张领航的地图
scene: 科学课上，小组把一周的气温记录画成了折线图贴在墙上。Our group drew a weather chart for the science class.
sceneCN: 这里 chart 是「图表」（第 1 个义项：把信息画成图形的纸）；句意为我们小组为科学课画了一张天气图表。

derivatives.zh: 由 chart 加 -ist 构成，历史上指靠图表研究行情的人
由 chart 加后缀构成，义为「无图表的；无海图的」

senses.title: A sheet showing facts as pictures or lines
senses.definition: a sheet of paper giving information in the form of pictures, lines or tables
senses.definitionCN: 用图形、线条或表格呈现信息的纸面
senses.example: Our group drew a weather chart for the science class.
senses.exampleCN: 我们小组为科学课画了一张天气图。
senses.why: A card was once any sheet of writing; when numbers are drawn instead of written, the sheet keeps the card's name.
senses.whyCN: card 本指写有文字的纸；当数字被画成图形，这张纸沿用了卡片的称呼。

senses.title: A map for sea or air travel
senses.definition: a map showing coasts, depths and dangers, used by sailors or pilots
senses.definitionCN: 标出海岸、水深与危险区域、供海员或飞行员使用的地图
senses.example: The captain studied the chart before leaving the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 船长出港前仔细研究海图。
senses.why: A sailing map is just a special sheet of drawn information, so it borrows the same name.
senses.whyCN: 航海地图就是一张特殊的「画出来的信息纸」，于是借用了同一个名字。

senses.title: A weekly list of the most popular songs
senses.definition: a published list showing the most popular songs or records each week
senses.definitionCN: 每周公布的流行歌曲或唱片的排名表
senses.example: Their new song jumped to the top of the charts.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的新歌蹿升到排行榜第一。
senses.why: A ranking list is again information drawn on a sheet, extending the drawn-sheet idea to popularity.
senses.whyCN: 排名表同样是「画在纸上的信息」，把图形纸的概念延伸到流行度上。

senses.title: To make a chart or plan something
senses.definition: to draw a chart of something, or to plan a course of action
senses.definitionCN: 为某物绘制图表，或规划行动路线
senses.example: The nurse charted the patient's temperature every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每小时把病人体温记录成表。
senses.why: Making the drawn sheet becomes an action verb, like turning any tool's name into using it.
senses.whyCN: 绘制图形纸的动作化为动词，正如工具名常转为使用它的动作。

intro.en: Chart and card share one Latin word for a sheet of papyrus, splitting into two English forms.
intro.cn: chart 与 card 同出一个拉丁语「莎草纸」词，在英语里分成两种形式。

items.en: Latin charta meant a leaf of papyrus or paper for writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 charta 指可供书写的莎草纸或纸张。

items.en: It came from Greek chartes, a sheet made from papyrus reeds.
items.cn: 该词源自希腊语 chartes，指用莎草制成的纸页。

items.en: Old French charte meant a document or map, especially one with authority.
items.cn: 古法语 charte 指文件或地图，尤指有权威性的文书。

items.en: Middle English took chart for a map, especially a sea map.
items.cn: 中古英语用 chart 指地图，尤指海图。

items.en: Modern English keeps the drawn-sheet senses: diagrams, sea maps and hit lists.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了图形纸的各义：图表、海图与排行榜。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects information-display words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收信息呈现类词。

entries.definition: A vehicle with wheels for carrying goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手推车」，拼写与 chart 相近。
名词，义为「甜菜叶」，拼写与 chart 相近。
名词，义为「宪章；特许状」，与 chart 同源。

entries.definition: A drawing showing how numbers change.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「曲线图」，与 chart 的图表义相近。

entries.definition: Facts arranged in rows and columns.

normalIntro.en: Remember chart by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 chart。

normal.en: chart comes from Latin charta, a sheet of paper.
normal.cn: chart 源自拉丁语 charta（纸张）。

normal.en: card is its twin word from the same root.
normal.cn: card 是同根的孪生词。

abstract.en: Picture bars of different heights marching across a grid.

abstract.en: Hear the captain's pen tracing coastlines on a map.

abstract.en: Feel a song climbing one step at a time to number one.
abstract.cn: 感受一首歌一步步爬上榜首的位置。

examples.en: Our group drew a weather chart for the science class.

examples.en: Their new song reached the top of the charts.

examples.en: The nurse charted the patient's temperature every hour.

definition_zh: 闲聊；聊天；闲谈
definition_en: to talk in a friendly, informal way; a friendly informal conversation
core_image: 两个朋友凑在一起，轻松随意地说着话
scene: 课间休息时，同桌凑过来聊起周末的篮球赛。We had a short chat about the basketball game during the break.
sceneCN: 这里 chat 是「闲聊」（第 1 个义项：轻松随意的谈话）；句意为课间我们聊了一会儿篮球赛。

derivatives.zh: 由 chat 加 -y 构成，义为「爱闲聊的；闲谈式的」
由 chat 加 room 构成，义为「聊天室」

senses.title: To talk in a friendly informal way
senses.definition: to talk with someone in a friendly, relaxed way about small things
senses.definitionCN: 以友好轻松的方式与人谈论日常小事
senses.example: We chatted about the basketball game after class.
senses.exampleCN: 课后我们聊起了篮球赛。
senses.why: The word pictures the light, repeated noise of small birds, matching easy small talk between friends.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原画的是小鸟轻快的鸣叫，正像朋友间轻松的闲话。

senses.title: A friendly informal conversation
senses.definition: a short, friendly and informal talk
senses.definitionCN: 一次短暂、友好且随意的谈话
senses.example: She gave me a quick chat before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前她和我快速聊了几句。
senses.why: The action of chatting easily names the talk itself, a normal move from act to event.
senses.whyCN: 闲聊的动作顺理成章命名了谈话本身，是常见的由行为转事件。

senses.title: Talking online by typing messages
senses.definition: exchanging typed messages with others on the internet in real time
senses.definitionCN: 通过互联网实时互发文字消息交流
senses.example: They chat in the class group every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每晚都在班级群里聊天。
senses.why: Typing on a screen feels like talking, so the old word of light talk moved onto the screen.
senses.whyCN: 在屏幕上打字如同说话，古老的轻谈一词便迁移到了屏幕上。

intro.en: Chat is a shortened, chirping form of chatter, first used for birds and then for people.
intro.cn: chat 是 chatter 的简短形式，最早形容鸟叫，后来用于人。

items.en: Old English ceatt was an echoic word, imitating small noises.
items.cn: 古英语 ceatt 是拟声词，模仿细碎的声音。

items.en: Middle English chater meant to make quick, repeated sounds, like birds or teeth.
items.cn: 中古英语 chater 指发出快速重复的声音，如鸟鸣或牙齿打颤。

items.en: Chatter applied to people talking rapidly about nothing important.
items.cn: chatter 开始形容人絮絮叨叨地谈琐事。

items.en: The short form chat appeared, meaning easy friendly talk.
items.cn: 简短形式 chat 出现，意为轻松友好的交谈。

items.en: Modern English chat covers spoken small talk and typed online talk.
items.cn: 现代英语的 chat 涵盖口头闲谈与在线文字聊天。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects talking words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收谈话类词。

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欺骗；作弊」，拼写与 chat 仅差一字母。

entries.definition: To talk quickly about unimportant things.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「喋喋不休」，由同根派生。

entries.definition: Something you wear on your head.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「帽子」，读音与 chat 词尾相近。
动词，义为「谈话」，泛指说话交流。

entries.definition: To talk about other people's private lives.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「闲话；说长道短」，与 chat 相近但略带贬义。

entries.definition: To talk with someone, more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「交谈」，较 chat 正式。

normalIntro.en: Remember chat by its root and family.

normal.en: chat is the short form of chatter.
normal.cn: chat 是 chatter 的简短形式。

normal.en: chatroom is where people chat online.
normal.cn: chatroom 是网上聊天的地方。

normal.en: chatty describes a talkative person.
normal.cn: chatty 形容爱聊天的人。

normal.en: have a chat is a natural everyday phrase.
normal.cn: have a chat 是地道的日常说法。

normal.en: birds chat too: the word first copied their sound.
normal.cn: 鸟也「聊天」：这个词最初就是模仿鸟叫。

abstract.en: Picture two birds trading quick little notes on a branch.
abstract.cn: 想象两只小鸟在枝头你来我往地短促鸣叫。

abstract.en: Hear soft laughter mixed into the lunchtime noise.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见午餐时间的喧闹里混着轻笑声。

abstract.en: Feel the message bubbles popping up one after another.
abstract.cn: 感受聊天气泡一条接一条弹出。

examples.en: We had a short chat about the basketball game during the break.
examples.cn: 课间我们简短地聊了一会儿篮球赛。

examples.en: She loves to chat with her friends on the way home.
examples.cn: 她喜欢在放学路上和朋友们聊天。

examples.en: They chatted in the class group until bedtime.
examples.cn: 他们在班级群里聊到睡觉时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「岔特」——话题岔来岔去特别多，这就是闲聊。

root: 拟声来源：古英语 ceatt（拟声）→ 中古英语 chater（喋喋不休）→ 短化形式 chat → 现代英语 chat；同族词有 chatter（喋喋不休）、chatty（爱闲谈的）。

sensesIntro.en: Chat moves from bird-like quick sounds to easy talk, the talk itself, and typed online talk.
sensesIntro.cn: chat 由鸟般的轻快叫声转为轻松谈话、谈话本身，再到在线文字交流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: quick light noise, like birds, between friends
core.cn: 核心意象：朋友间如鸟鸣般轻快的细碎声音

intro.en: Chat is an echoic word, born from sound rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: chat 是拟声词，源于声音而非拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: It has no Latin relatives; its family is the echoic chatter group.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁同族词，词族是拟声的 chatter 一系。

items.example: The girls chattered about the film.
items.exampleCN: 女孩们叽叽喳喳聊电影。

items.example: She is bright and chatty.
The old chatrooms are quiet now.

definition_zh: 便宜的；廉价的；劣质的；小气的
definition_en: costing little money; of low quality; unwilling to spend money
core_image: 价签上小小的数字，或一扯就坏的劣质玩具
scene: 文具店里，弟弟对比了两支笔的价签，挑了便宜的那支。He picked the cheaper pen because it cost less money.
sceneCN: 这里 cheap 是「便宜的」（第 1 个义项：花钱少）；句意为他选了更便宜的笔，因为花的钱少。

derivatives.zh: 由 cheap 加 -ly 构成，义为「便宜地」
由 cheap 加 -ness 构成，义为「便宜；廉价」
由 cheap 加 -en 构成，义为「降价；使贬值」

senses.title: Costing little money
senses.definition: not costing a lot of money; low in price
senses.definitionCN: 价钱不高；花钱少
senses.example: The cheaper pen costs only two yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 那支便宜的笔只卖两块钱。
senses.why: Old English named the price-setting market-place; goods traded there came to be called by the place of their price.
senses.whyCN: 古英语本指定价的集市；在集市上成交的货物便以「定价之地」来称呼。

senses.title: Of low quality
senses.definition: of low quality, made or done without care
senses.definitionCN: 质量低劣，做工粗糙
senses.example: The cheap toy broke on the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 那个廉价玩具第一天就坏了。
senses.why: Goods priced very low often give less quality, so the low price sense slid into low quality.
senses.whyCN: 定价极低的货往往做工欠佳，「价低」便滑向「质劣」。

senses.title: Not willing to spend money
senses.definition: unwilling to spend money; not generous
senses.definitionCN: 不愿花钱；不慷慨
senses.example: He felt too cheap to buy his friends a drink.
senses.exampleCN: 他小气得不愿请朋友喝东西。
senses.why: Someone who always picks the lowest cost looks mean, so the price word turned to describe the person.
senses.whyCN: 总挑最便宜价的人显得吝啬，价格词于是转而形容人。

senses.title: Feeling ashamed or worthless
senses.definition: feeling embarrassed or of little value
senses.definitionCN: 感到难为情或自觉不值钱
senses.example: She felt cheap after telling the lie.
senses.exampleCN: 撒谎之后她觉得羞愧。
senses.why: A person of low price feels low, extending the value picture to one's inner worth.
senses.whyCN: 「价格低」的人自我感觉低贱，价值画面被延伸到内心的自尊上。

intro.en: Cheap began as the name of a market-place and moved on to the price of goods sold there.
intro.cn: cheap 起初是集市之名，后来转指集市上货物所定的价格。

items.en: Latin caupo meant a small trader or innkeeper who sold things.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caupo 指小商贩或客栈老板。

items.en: Early Germanic borrowed it as a word for trade or a trader.
items.cn: 早期日耳曼语借入，指交易或商人。

items.en: Old English ceap meant trade, a purchase, or the market where trading happened.
items.cn: 古英语 ceap 指交易、买卖，也指进行买卖的集市。

items.en: In Middle English, good cep meant a good bargain, and market-places kept names like Cheapside.
items.cn: 中古英语 good cep 意为划算的交易；伦敦 Cheapside（菜市场街）等地名留存至今。

items.en: Modern English settled on the price sense: cheap means costing little.
items.cn: 现代英语固定于价格义：cheap 表示花销少。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects price words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收价格类词。

abstract.cn: 想象集市的风里飘着一枚小小的价签。

abstract.en: Hear the haggling noise of an old English market street.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见古英语集市街上的讨价还价声。

abstract.en: Feel a thin toy cracking between your fingers.
abstract.cn: 感受薄脆的玩具在指间裂开。

examples.cn: 他挑了更便宜的笔，因为花的钱少。

examples.cn: 那个廉价玩具第一天就坏了。

examples.en: She felt cheap after copying the homework.
examples.cn: 抄作业之后她感到羞愧。

latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁祖先 caupo 指小商贩。

items.example: The cheapness of the shoes surprised me.

definition_zh: 检查；核对；阻止；控制；支票；（下棋）将军
definition_en: to examine something to make sure it is right or safe; to stop something; a bill or written order to pay
core_image: 落子前先停一停，把每一步都看清楚再放行
scene: 交卷之前，班长提醒大家先核对一遍名字和题号。Please check your answers before you hand in the paper.
sceneCN: 这里 check 是「检查；核对」（第 1 个义项：查验以确保无误）；句意为交卷前请先核对答案。

derivatives.zh: 由 check 加 -er 构成，义为「检查员；检验器」
由 check 加 out 构成，义为「结账处；检验」
由 check 加 list 构成，义为「核对清单」

senses.title: To examine to make sure all is right
senses.definition: to look at something carefully to be sure it is correct, safe or complete
senses.definitionCN: 仔细查看以确保正确、安全或完整
senses.example: Please check your answers before handing in the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 交卷前请核对答案。
senses.why: The chess call for a threat made players look twice, and looking twice became examining anything carefully.
senses.whyCN: 象棋中「将军」的喊声让人反复确认，反复确认便成了仔细查验。

senses.title: To stop something from growing or moving
senses.definition: to hold something back so it cannot grow or move freely
senses.definitionCN: 牵制某物，使其不能自由增长或行动
senses.example: The fence checks the wind across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 围栏挡住了田野上的风。
senses.why: In chess, a checked king cannot move freely; anything held back by a threat is likewise checked.
senses.whyCN: 象棋里被将军的王寸步难行；被威胁所牵制之物同样被「将」住了。

senses.title: A written order to pay money
senses.definition: a printed form telling a bank to pay money from your account
senses.definitionCN: 通知银行从账户付款的印制单据
senses.example: Grandpa paid the fee by cheque.
senses.exampleCN: 爷爷用支票付了费用。
senses.why: A bank paper 'checks' the account: it calls for the money to be examined and handed over.
senses.whyCN: 银行单据「查验」账户：要求核对后将款项交付。

senses.title: A bill in a restaurant
senses.definition: the written bill for food or services in a restaurant
senses.definitionCN: 餐馆里写明餐费的单据
senses.example: Let me see the check, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请把账单给我看看。
senses.why: The bill is the paper that lets you examine and settle what you owe.
senses.whyCN: 账单就是让你核对并结清所欠款项的那张纸。

senses.title: A pattern of squares, or a mark of correctness
senses.definition: a pattern of crossed squares, or a mark showing something has been examined
senses.definitionCN: 交叉的方格图案，或表示已查验的记号
senses.example: The teacher put a check beside each correct answer.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在每道正确答案旁打了勾。
senses.why: Marking an examined item with a tick, like squares on a board, fixes the examining sense into a visible sign.
senses.whyCN: 用记号标注已查过的项目，如同棋盘上的方格，把查验之义固定成可见的符号。

intro.en: Check comes from the game of chess: the call shah, 'the king is threatened', travelled through Persian into everyday English.
intro.cn: check 源自国际象棋：波斯语的「王被将」呼语一路传入日常英语。

items.en: Persian shah means king; shah mat gave the chess phrase for a trapped king.
items.cn: 波斯语 shah 意为国王；shah mat 是棋语中被困之王的呼语。

items.en: Old French eschec meant the call in chess and any setback or check.
items.cn: 古法语 eschec 指象棋中的将军呼语，也指挫败。

items.en: Middle English chek kept the chess sense and grew the sense of stopping or rebuke.
items.cn: 中古英语 chek 保留棋义，并发展出阻止、惩戒之义。

items.en: Senses multiplied: examining, controlling, bank cheques, square patterns.
items.cn: 义项倍增：查验、控制、银行支票、方格图案。

items.en: American spelling chose check for both the bank paper and the examining sense.
items.cn: 美式拼写用 check 兼指支票与查验之义。

definition_zh: 欢呼；喝彩；鼓舞；使高兴；欢呼声；愉快
definition_en: to shout with joy or support; to make someone happier; a shout of joy; a feeling of happiness
core_image: 看台上齐声呐喊为队伍加油，把低落的士气重新点亮
scene: 运动会接力赛上，全班在终点线旁为最后一棒呐喊助威。The whole class began to cheer for the last runner.
sceneCN: 这里 cheer 是「欢呼；加油」（第 1 个义项：喊出支持与喜悦的声音）；句意为全班为最后一棒呐喊助威。

derivatives.zh: 由 cheer 加 -ful 构成，义为「快乐的；令人愉快的」
由 cheer 加 leader 构成，义为「啦啦队长；支持者」
由 cheer 加 -y 构成，义为「兴高采烈的」

senses.title: To shout with joy or support
senses.definition: to shout loudly to show joy or to encourage a person or team
senses.definitionCN: 大声呼喊以表达喜悦或为人和队伍鼓劲
senses.example: The whole class began to cheer for the last runner.
senses.exampleCN: 全班开始为最后一棒呐喊助威。
senses.why: The word first named the expression on the face; when a crowd's joy bursts out, the face's word becomes the shout.
senses.whyCN: 词最初指脸上的神情；当人群的喜悦迸发而出，表情之名便化作呐喊之声。

senses.title: To make someone happier
senses.definition: to make a sad or tired person feel better
senses.definitionCN: 让难过或疲惫的人好受起来
senses.example: A hot meal cheered the tired players.
senses.exampleCN: 一顿热饭让疲惫的队员精神一振。
senses.why: Bringing joy to one face is the inward side of the outward shout: same feeling, quieter form.
senses.whyCN: 把喜悦带到一张脸上，正是欢呼声的内敛一面：同一种情感，更安静的形式。

senses.title: A shout of encouragement or joy
senses.definition: a loud shout of joy or support from a group
senses.definitionCN: 人群发出的喜悦或支持的呐喊
senses.example: A great cheer went up when the goal was scored.
senses.exampleCN: 进球时爆发出一片欢呼。
senses.why: The act of shouting is named, then the sound itself keeps the same name.
senses.whyCN: 呼喊的动作先被命名，喊出的声音随后沿用其名。

senses.title: A mood of happiness
senses.definition: a feeling of happiness and hope
senses.definitionCN: 快乐与希望的心情
senses.example: Her kind words filled the room with cheer.
senses.exampleCN: 她温暖的话语让满屋生辉。
senses.why: Behind both shout and smile sits the feeling itself, and the word can name that feeling alone.
senses.whyCN: 呼喊与笑容背后是情感本身，这个词也能单独指称这份心情。

intro.en: Cheer once meant the face or expression, then the inner mood, then the loud joy that shows both.
intro.cn: cheer 最初指面容神情，继而指内心情绪，最后指表露二者的欢腾。

items.en: Late Latin cara meant the face, from Greek kara, the head.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cara 指面容，源自希腊语 kara（头）。

items.en: Old French chere meant the face and the expression shown on it.
items.cn: 古法语 chere 指面容及其流露的神情。

items.en: Middle English chere meant expression, then mood: of good chere meant happy.
items.cn: 中古英语 chere 指神情，继而指心情；of good chere 即心情愉悦。

items.en: The sense moved outward to shouts of welcome and joy.
items.cn: 词义外移，指欢迎与喜悦的呼喊。

items.en: Modern English keeps the shout, the encouragement and the happy mood.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了欢呼、鼓舞与愉快心情诸义。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects joy and support words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收喜悦与支持类词。

definition_zh: 快乐的；令人愉快的；乐意的
definition_en: happy and smiling; making people feel happy; said in a happy way
core_image: 脸上挂着阳光般的笑，走进房间就把气氛点亮
scene: 值日生擦完黑板，笑眯眯地回到座位，连老师都被感染了。She gave a cheerful smile when she finished cleaning the board.
sceneCN: 这里 cheerful 是「快乐的」（第 1 个义项：面带笑容、心情好）；句意为她擦完黑板后露出快乐的微笑。

senses.title: Happy and smiling
senses.definition: feeling or showing happiness, with a smile
senses.definitionCN: 感到或显出快乐，面带笑容
senses.example: She gave a cheerful smile when she finished cleaning the board.
senses.exampleCN: 她擦完黑板后露出快乐的微笑。
senses.why: The word piles the happy mood onto the face that shows it, matching its old meaning of expression.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把快乐的情绪叠加在显露它的脸上，正与其古义「神情」相合。

senses.title: Making people feel happy
senses.definition: making a place or time feel bright and happy
senses.definitionCN: 让地方或时光显得明亮快乐
senses.example: The yellow curtains make the room cheerful.
senses.exampleCN: 黄色的窗帘让房间显得明快。
senses.why: A thing that fills a room with the happy feeling borrows the mood word for itself.
senses.whyCN: 让房间充满快乐情绪之物，便借用了这种情绪词来描述自身。

senses.title: Said or done in a willing, bright way
senses.definition: willing and happy to do something, without complaining
senses.definitionCN: 乐意且愉快地做某事，毫无怨言
senses.example: He gave a cheerful yes to the extra job.
senses.exampleCN: 他爽快地答应接下额外的活儿。
senses.why: A person with a bright mood agrees easily, so the mood word extends to willing action.
senses.whyCN: 心情明亮的人答应得爽快，情绪词便延伸到乐于做事的态度上。

definition_en: a solid food made from milk, pressed into blocks and left to ripen

senses.title: A solid food made from milk
senses.definition: a food made by pressing and ripening the thick part of milk

senses.example: The hard cheese was cut into thin slices for the sandwiches.
senses.exampleCN: 硬奶酪被切成薄片夹进三明治。
senses.why: The word names the pressed milk product directly, by what it is made of and how it is made.

senses.title: A specific kind or shape of cheese

senses.example: Many soft cheeses come from France.

senses.whyCN: 泛指的产品容易分化为品种，各品种沿用产品之名再配新修饰语。

senses.title: A smile posed for a photo
senses.definition: the forced smile people make when a photographer says 'say cheese'

definition_zh: 化学的；化学制品；化学品

senses.title: A substance used in chemistry

senses.title: Connected with the science of substances

senses.title: Made by chemical processes, not natural

intro.en: Chemical is built on chemistry, whose own story starts in the old craft of alchemy.
intro.cn: chemical 建立在 chemistry 之上，而后者的历史可追溯到古老的炼金术。

items.en: The root of alchemy is uncertain: Egyptian keme (black earth), Greek chuma (pouring) and Arabic al-kimiya are all proposed sources.
items.cn: alchemy 的词根存疑：埃及语 keme（黑土）、希腊语 chuma（浇注）与阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 均为候选来源。

items.en: Medieval Latin alchemia meant alchemy, the craft of changing matter.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchemia 指炼金术，即转变物质的技艺。

items.en: French chimie separated the science of substances from the old magic craft.
items.cn: 法语 chimie 把物质之学与古老的秘术区分开来。

items.en: English chemistry, then chemical, named the science and its materials.
items.cn: 英语依次出现 chemistry 与 chemical，命名这门学科及其材料。

items.en: The adjective chemical settled for scientific change, and chemicals for the substances.
items.cn: 形容词 chemical 定型于科学变化，chemicals 指各类化学物质。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects science and substance words.

normalIntro.en: Remember chemical by its root and family.

normal.cn: chemist 既指化学家，在英式英语里也指药剂师。

normal.cn: alchemist（炼金术士）是更古老的词，指寻找黄金之人。

normal.en: farm chemicals help crops grow but must be used with care.
normal.cn: 农用化学品帮助庄稼生长，但须谨慎使用。

abstract.en: Picture coloured liquids bubbling quietly in test tubes.
abstract.cn: 想象试管里彩色液体静静冒泡。

abstract.en: Hear the small pop when two drops meet.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见两滴液体相遇时轻微的爆裂声。

abstract.en: Feel the cool glass of a labelled bottle in your hand.
abstract.cn: 感受贴着标签的试剂瓶冰凉的玻璃瓶身。

sensesIntro.cn: chemical 由学科形容词延伸到化学物质与人工合成品。

core.cn: 核心意象：化学所研究与制造的物质

root: 波斯语 shah（王）→ 古法语 eschec → 中古英语 chek → 现代英语 check / cheque；同根词有 checkmate（将死）、chess（国际象棋）、checker（检查员）。

sensesIntro.en: Cheque moves from a chess call to a bank paper, a restaurant bill and unlimited permission.
sensesIntro.cn: cheque 由象棋呼语到银行单据、餐馆账单与无限授权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a paper that orders the bank to pay
core.cn: 核心意象：一张命令银行付款的纸

intro.en: Cheque is check dressed in a French-style spelling.
intro.cn: cheque 是 check 的法式拼写变体。

latinIntro.en: It has no Latin root; its line runs from Persian through chess.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁词根，源自波斯语经象棋一路传播。

items.example: He opened his chequebook.
Many bills are paid by cheque.

items.meaning: to exchange a cheque for money
items.example: Cash the cheque at the bank.

items.meaning: a cheque without an amount; full freedom
items.example: The plan got a blank cheque.
The rent cheque bounced.
Show your cheque card when paying.
items.exampleCN: 付款时出示支票保证卡。

items.meaning: a cheque payable only through a bank
items.meaningCN: 划线支票（只能经银行转账）
items.example: A crossed cheque is safer to post.
Travel cheques are safer than cash.

definition_zh: 胸；胸腔；箱子；柜子
definition_en: the upper front part of the body between the neck and the stomach; a large strong box with a lid for storing things
core_image: 厚木箱扣着大铁锁，或胸膛起伏的一次深呼吸
scene: 体育课跑完四百米，同学们手按胸口大口喘气。After the 400-metre run, we all held our chests and panted.
sceneCN: 这里 chest 是「胸」（第 1 个义项：颈到胃之间的身体前部）；句意为跑完四百米后大家手按胸口喘气。

derivatives.zh: 由 chest 加 -y 构成，义为「胸部不适的；（咳嗽）带痰音的」
由 chest（古义）加 nut 构成，义为「栗子；栗树」

senses.title: The upper front part of the body
senses.definition: the front upper part of the body between the neck and the stomach
senses.definitionCN: 颈部与胃部之间的身体前上部
senses.example: After the 400-metre run, we all held our chests and panted.
senses.exampleCN: 跑完四百米后，大家都手按胸口喘气。
senses.why: The body's front box that holds the heart and lungs was named after the box that holds treasures.
senses.whyCN: 盛着心与肺的身体前箱，因盛放珍宝的箱子而得名。

senses.title: A large strong box with a lid
senses.definition: a large, strong box with a lid, used for storing or carrying things
senses.definitionCN: 带盖的大型坚固箱子，用于储存或搬运
senses.example: The old wooden chest in the attic holds winter clothes.
senses.exampleCN: 阁楼上的旧木箱装着过冬衣物。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the container itself: a strong box that keeps things safe inside.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是容器本身：一只把物品妥善收藏的坚固木箱。

senses.title: A set of drawers for storing clothes
senses.definition: a piece of furniture with drawers for storing clothes
senses.definitionCN: 带抽屉用于存放衣物的家具
senses.example: She folded the shirts into the chest of drawers.
senses.exampleCN: 她把衬衫叠好放进五斗柜。
senses.why: The storing box grew furniture-like, divided into drawers that still 'keep' things.
senses.whyCN: 储物之箱逐渐家具化，分成一只只仍司「收纳」之职的抽屉。

senses.title: The box-like middle of the body in speech
senses.definition: the chest as the seat of feelings or strength
senses.definitionCN: 作为情感或力量所在的胸膛
senses.example: He beat his chest after winning the race.
senses.exampleCN: 赢得比赛后他捶胸欢呼。
senses.why: Because the chest visibly rises with strong feeling, it stands for feeling itself.
senses.whyCN: 胸膛随强烈情绪明显起伏，便被借代为情感本身。

intro.en: Chest began as a word for a strong box, and the body part borrowed the container's name.
intro.cn: chest 起初指坚固的箱子，身体部位借用了这个容器的名字。

items.en: Old English cest meant a box or basket for storing things.
items.cn: 古英语 cest 指储物的箱子或篮子。

items.en: It goes back to Latin cista, a woven box or basket.
items.cn: 其源头是拉丁语 cista，指编织的箱篮。

items.en: Latin cista came from Greek kiste, a woven chest.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cista 又源自希腊语 kiste（编织箱）。

items.en: Middle English chest named the box and, by likeness, the rib cage.
items.cn: 中古英语 chest 既指箱子，又因形似转指胸廓。

items.en: Modern English chest covers the body part, the box and the drawer furniture.
items.cn: 现代英语的 chest 兼指身体部位、箱柜与抽屉家具。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects containers and body words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收纳物与身体类词。

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欺骗」，拼写与 chest 相近。

entries.definition: A board game for two players.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「国际象棋」，读音与 chest 词首相近。
名词，义为「栗子」，由 chest 古义加 nut 构成。
名词，义为「胸（前部）」，与 chest 意义相近。

entries.definition: A large travelling box; the torso.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大旅行箱；躯干」，兼有箱与身躯二义。

entries.definition: One of the curved bones protecting the chest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肋骨」，构成胸腔的骨架。

normalIntro.en: Remember chest by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 chest。

normal.en: chest first meant a strong box.
normal.cn: chest 最先指坚固的箱子。

normal.en: chestnut is the nut of the old box word.
normal.cn: chestnut（栗子）用的正是「箱子」的古义。

normal.en: a chest of drawers stores folded clothes.
normal.cn: chest of drawers 用于存放叠好的衣物。

normal.en: treasure chest is the pirate's dream box.
normal.cn: treasure chest（宝箱）是海盗梦寐以求的箱子。

normal.en: your chest is the box that holds heart and lungs.
normal.cn: 胸腔就是盛着心肺的「箱子」。

abstract.en: Picture a locked oak box deep in the attic.
abstract.cn: 想象阁楼深处一把上锁的橡木箱。

abstract.en: Hear the steady drum of breath after a long run.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见长跑后胸口平稳有力的起伏鼓点。

abstract.en: Feel ribs closing around the lungs like box walls.
abstract.cn: 感受肋骨如箱壁般护住双肺。

examples.en: After the 400-metre run, we all held our chests and panted.
examples.cn: 跑完四百米后，大家都手按胸口喘气。

examples.en: The old wooden chest in the attic holds winter clothes.
examples.cn: 阁楼上的旧木箱装着过冬衣物。

examples.en: The doctor listened to his chest with a stethoscope.
examples.cn: 医生用听诊器听了他的胸腔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拆死它」——想拆开宝箱？先过我的胸膛。

root: 希腊语 kiste（编织箱）→ 拉丁语 cista（箱篮）→ 古英语 cest（箱子）→ 现代英语 chest；同族词有 chestnut（栗子）、chesty（胸部不适的）。

sensesIntro.en: Chest moves from a strong box to the body's box, drawer furniture and the seat of feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: chest 由坚固木箱延伸到身体之箱、抽屉柜与情感之所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strong box that keeps things in
core.cn: 核心意象：把物品牢牢收住的坚固箱匣

intro.en: Chest keeps the ancient woven-box root kist- in its short form.
intro.cn: chest 的短词形里保留了古老的编织箱词根 kist-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cista and Greek kiste are its ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cista 与希腊语 kiste 是其祖先。

items.example: The first chest was woven from rushes.
items.exampleCN: 最早的箱子用灯芯草编成。

items.meaning: the nut of the chestnut tree
items.example: We roasted chestnuts in autumn.
A chesty cough kept him home.
The story told of a treasure chest.
The socks live in the chest of drawers.
Tell the teacher about any chest pain.

items.meaning: money saved for a big effort
items.example: The team built up a war chest.
items.exampleCN: 团队攒下了一笔专项基金。

items.example: Archaeologists found a stone cist.
items.exampleCN: 考古学家发现了一座石柜墓。

definition_zh: 鸡；小鸡；鸡肉；胆小鬼
definition_en: a farm bird kept for eggs and meat; the meat of this bird; a person who is afraid to do something
core_image: 院子里咯咯叫的母鸡，或饭桌上一盘香喷喷的炸鸡
scene: 放学路上经过农场，几只小鸡正跟着母鸡在草地上找虫子。The chickens followed the hen across the farmyard.
sceneCN: 这里 chicken 是「鸡；小鸡」（第 1 个义项：家养禽鸟）；句意为小鸡们跟着母鸡穿过农场院子。

derivatives.zh: 由 chicken 加 hearted 构成，义为「胆小的」
由 chicken 加 coop 构成，义为「鸡舍」

senses.title: A farm bird kept for eggs and meat
senses.definition: a common farm bird with feathers, kept for its eggs and meat
senses.definitionCN: 常见的家养禽鸟，人们养它取蛋和取肉
senses.example: The chickens followed the hen across the farmyard.
senses.exampleCN: 小鸡们跟着母鸡穿过农场院子。
senses.why: The baby-bird word grew into the general name of the farm bird at every age.
senses.whyCN: 幼雏之义逐渐扩大，成为家禽在各个年龄段的统称。

senses.title: The meat of this bird
senses.definition: the meat of a chicken, eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物的鸡肉
senses.example: Grandma cooked chicken soup for the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶给全家炖了鸡汤。
senses.why: The animal's name easily becomes the name of the dish on the table.
senses.whyCN: 禽鸟之名顺理成章变为餐桌菜肴之名。

senses.title: A person who is afraid to do something
senses.definition: a person who is too frightened to do something
senses.definitionCN: 因害怕而不敢做某事的人
senses.example: Don't be a chicken; jump into the pool!
senses.exampleCN: 别当胆小鬼，跳进泳池吧！
senses.why: A young bird flapping and fleeing at everything became the picture of a timid person.
senses.whyCN: 小鸡稍有风吹草动便扑翅而逃，便成了胆小之人的写照。

senses.title: Feeling or showing fear
senses.definition: afraid to do something
senses.definitionCN: 不敢做某事的
senses.example: He felt chicken about speaking on stage.
senses.exampleCN: 他害怕上台发言。
senses.why: The timid-bird picture works as an adjective for fearful behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 怯懦小鸟的画面用作形容词，描述害怕的行为。

intro.en: Chicken began as the word for a young bird and grew into the farm bird, its meat and the timid person.
intro.cn: chicken 起初指幼雏，逐渐扩展为家禽、鸡肉与胆小之人。

items.en: Old English cicen meant a young bird, especially a young hen.
items.cn: 古英语 cicen 指幼鸟，尤指小母鸡。

items.en: It traces to a Germanic root for a young bird, kak-, echoing its chirp.
items.cn: 其可追溯至日耳曼语幼鸟词根 kak-，拟声其叫声。

items.en: Middle English chiken named the young bird and, by extension, the bird at any age.
items.cn: 中古英语 chiken 指幼雏，进而泛指各年龄段的鸡。

items.en: The meat sense and the timid-person sense both spread in everyday speech.
items.cn: 肉类义与胆小者之义都在日常口语中扩散。

items.en: Modern English chicken is a farm bird, a dish, and a dare word among friends.
items.cn: 现代英语的 chicken 既是家禽、菜肴，也是朋友间激将用词。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects farm birds and timidity words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收家禽与怯懦类词。

normal.cn: chick 是其幼鸟简称。
